title: Finite Tor dimension on affine opens of a relatively flat proper image
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be proper, locally of finite presentation and quasi-compact, and $F$ a finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-module flat over $f$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions, def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Supply independent derived localizations on $X$ and $S$ [def-pc-derived-category]. For any affine open $U\subseteq S$ with a derived localization in the target morphism universe, the exact open restriction [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps] of $Rf_*(F[0])$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] has finite Tor dimension on $U$ [def-pc-finite-tor-dimension]: one interval $[a,b]$ with $a\le b$ bounds its derived tensor cohomology with every $\mathcal O_U$-module. Bounds may vary with $U$. No pseudo-coherence, finite-free representative or perfection is asserted.

source.place: Tags 01XD (coherent-lemma-cech-cohomology-quasi-coherent), 08FE (cohomology-lemma-restrict-direct-image-open), 08CG and 08CI; finite-flat-Cech part of Tag 0A1H

proof.text: Over the supplied affine U, quasi-compactness gives a finite affine cover of the inverse image. Properness gives separatedness. Restrict relative flatness by the section-ring identifications for open inclusions. Form the actual finiteAffineCechModel. Its degree bounds are 0 and the size of the finite cover; its terms are flat over the identity by the finite-affine-Cech flatness theorem.

The finite affine Cech derived comparison identifies Q of this specified complex with the restricted morphism direct image of the restricted single module. The open direct-image comparison and the exact-restriction-single comparison identify it with the requested open restriction of Rf_*(F[0]). Use the standard localization on the inverse-image scheme; the two comparisons allow independent source and target localizations.

Flatness over the identity implies tensor-exact sheaf flatness. The complex is bounded above, hence K-flat. For any module M, tensoring the complex with M[0] is isomorphic to termwise tensor. Outside the bounds its degree-n term is zero; tensor preserves zero objects, and a zero middle term in the homology short complex gives zero homology. The same interval [0,r] works for all M, so use this complex and the preceding representing isomorphism in the definition of finite Tor dimension. Empty covers and zero modules give zero terms.

theorem properFlat_single_local_hasFiniteTorDimension
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wS}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace))]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] (hF : F.IsFlatOver f)
    (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wS}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))] :
    U.toScheme.HasFiniteTorDimension ((schemeOpenRestriction S U).mapDerivedCategory.obj
      ((schemeDerivedDirectImage f).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj F)))
